title: How to write a warranty letter after a roofing job
summary: Paste what you actually guarantee into ChatGPT and get a plain warranty letter after a roofing job. Check the coverage and the term before you send it.

tests.prompt:
You help a roofer write a warranty letter after a finished job. Draft only. Do not send it.

Fill in these details. If a line is blank, write UNKNOWN and do not guess.

Customer name: [CUSTOMER NAME]
Job address: [JOB ADDRESS]
Work completed: [WORK]
Completion date: [COMPLETION DATE]
What the warranty covers: [COVERS]
How long it lasts: [TERM]
What it does not cover: [NOT COVERED]
How to make a warranty request: [HOW TO CLAIM]
Your name and business: [YOUR NAME]
Your phone: [YOUR PHONE]
Email or text: [CHANNEL]

Rules:
- Never invent details; if something is missing, ask or mark it UNKNOWN.
- Do not invent a warranty length, a manufacturer name, or a coverage item.
- Do not promise work-or-materials coverage you did not type in.
- Do not use legal jargon. Write a plain letter a homeowner can keep with their paperwork.
- If [TERM] or [COVERS] is blank, mark it UNKNOWN. Do not guess "one year" or "lifetime."
- No marketing language and no upsell.

Output format:
Return these headings only:
Channel
Subject (NONE if this is a text)
Letter (200 words or fewer)
What is covered
What is not covered
How to request service
Facts used
Unknown

setup.agent: Paste this into ChatGPT, or into the chat assistant you already use.
steps: Write the customer name, address, the work you completed, the completion date, what you cover, how long it lasts, and what you do not cover.
Add how they should request service, your name, phone, and whether this is an email or a letter you will paste into email.
Open ChatGPT, paste the ChatGPT prompt, and replace every [BRACKET]. Type UNKNOWN if you still need to confirm a term with your supplier.
Check the coverage, the term, and the exclusions against the terms you actually offer. Delete any lifetime language or manufacturer claim you did not write down.
Send the letter by email or print it with the final invoice, yourself, after those terms match.
setup.approvalStep: You check the coverage and the term against what you actually guarantee, then you send the letter yourself.
failureModes: The draft invents a one-year, five-year, or lifetime term. Put only your real term back in.
Manufacturer warranty language appears that you did not provide. Leave it out or add the exact terms from the manufacturer sheet.
Exclusions you rely on, such as storm damage or owner-made changes, are missing. Add them from your notes before you send.
The completion date or address is wrong. Match the job file.

faq.q: Should I also mention the shingle manufacturer's warranty?
faq.a: Only if you have the official terms and you add them to the details. Do not guess the manufacturer's length or coverage.

faq.q: What if I do not offer a workmanship warranty?
faq.a: Do not send this letter. A warranty letter should only go out when you have terms you will honor.

faq.q: Can this create a legal warranty document?
faq.a: It writes a plain letter that restates the terms you typed in. If you need a formal legal document, have someone qualified review it. Do not let the draft invent legal language.

job: Paste your real warranty terms and get a plain letter a homeowner can keep after a roofing job.
who: Roofers who want a short, honest warranty letter that matches the workmanship they actually stand behind.

example.scenario: A roofer finished a shingle replacement and wants to email a workmanship warranty with the final invoice.
example.input:
Customer name: Sam Rivera
Job address: 14 Pine Street
Work completed: Full tear-off and new architectural shingles
Completion date: April 16, 2026
What the warranty covers: Our workmanship, including leaks caused by our installation
How long it lasts: 5 years from the completion date
What it does not cover: Storm damage, acts of nature, and changes made by anyone other than our crew
How to make a warranty request: Call or email us, and we will come look at it
Your name and business: Jordan at Ridge Line Roofing
Your phone: 555-0172
Email or text: email
example.output:
Channel: email
Subject: Warranty letter for the roof at 14 Pine Street

Letter:
Hi Sam, this is Jordan at Ridge Line Roofing. Thank you again for the work at 14 Pine Street. We completed the full tear-off and new architectural shingles on April 16, 2026. This letter is the workmanship warranty for that job.

What is covered: Our workmanship, including leaks caused by our installation, for 5 years from April 16, 2026.

What is not covered: Storm damage, acts of nature, and changes made by anyone other than our crew.

How to request service: Call or email Ridge Line Roofing at 555-0172 and we will come look at it.

Please keep this letter with your job paperwork. If anything in the coverage is unclear, call me and I will walk you through it.

Facts used: 14 Pine Street, April 16, 2026, 5 years, workmanship, storm damage excluded.
Unknown: none.
example.notes: Made-up warranty terms, only to show a plain letter. Use only the terms you actually offer.
